datasource_item.query: Shipment SHIP-VC-1026-BOS-FRA exceeded its temperature range. What happened, and can the 4,800 units be distributed?
datasource_item.ground_truth: The shipment had a 150-minute high-temperature excursion during the Frankfurt transfer and reached 10.7 C. The 4,800 units were quarantined, reviewed against the approved stability allowance, and released for distribution.
datasource_item.sample.output_text:
Shipment **SHIP-VC-1026-BOS-FRA** had a **high-temperature excursion** in the **Frankfurt airport controlled-transfer area** during transfer from the aircraft container to refrigerated road transport, when temperature rose above the validated **2.0–8.0 °C** range to a maximum of **10.7 °C** for **2 hr 30 min** from **15 Oct 2026 08:30 UTC to 11:00 UTC** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1; TL-VCL-1026.pdf, Page 1].

What happened:
- The investigation states the **probable cause** was that the **active air container remained at the controlled-transfer bay for 94 minutes beyond the validated handoff window after a ground-handler vehicle change** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- A **contributing factor** was that the **replacement refrigerated vehicle arrived after the scheduled connection window** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- The packaging was reported as **intact**, with **no opening or physical damage observed**, and proof of delivery recorded **no visible shipper damage** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2; EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].

Affected quantity:
- The affected inventory was **12 insulated cartons (4,800 units)** from **lot CLD-VCL-1026-A** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].

Can the 4,800 units be distributed?
- **Initially, no**: the units were placed in **physical quarantine** and labeled **“QUARANTINE – DO NOT DISTRIBUTE”** pending assessment [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].
- **Final disposition: yes**. The quality assessment concluded that the **recorded exposure remained within the approved stability allowance for lot CLD-VCL-1026-A** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- The final report explicitly states **“Released for distribution”**, quarantine was removed on **16 Oct 2026 18:10 UTC**, and the product **“may proceed through the authorized distribution channel”** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].

So, based on the retrieved evidence, the shipment experienced a transfer-delay-driven temperature excursion, but the specific affected lot **CLD-VCL-1026-A** was **formally released for distribution after quality review and customer disposition approval** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].

function_call_output.title: GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf
function_call_output.content:
SYSTEM INSPECTION ASSESSMENT
RATING
Pharmaceutical quality system The site initiated deviation controls promptly and notified Caldova within the quality-agreement timeline. Investigation governance was weakened by late Quality involvement in maintenance evidence review and by an initial root-cause statement issued before the connection was disassembled.
Improvement required
Personnel and training Operators interviewed understood line clearance and aseptic response expectations. Two of six maintenance technicians had not completed the revision-6 practical assessment for sanitary gasket installation before performing independent work.
Deficient
Premises and equipment BR-04 was orderly and appropriately segregated. TC-4 is positioned below an overhead return bend, limiting direct visual confirmation of gasket seating after assembly. No inspection mirror or borescope step was specified.
Deficient
Production and in-process controls Manufacturing records showed expected upstream controls and timely isolation. The closed transfer path was released to service without documented evidence that the required pressure-hold acceptance criterion had been met.
Deficient
Laboratory control Microbiology methods, controls, and sample traceability reviewed were acceptable. Localization of the positive result downstream of TC-4 and the negative retained upstream sample were scientifically coherent with the identified breach.
Acceptable
Documentation and data governance The maintenance system permitted closure of WO-BPB-1026-441 while the linked pressure-hold result field was blank. The audit trail recorded the omission but did not trigger supervisory escalation.
Deficient
Materials, sanitation, and hygiene Gasket receipt, storage, status labeling, cleaning, and personnel gowning controls sampled were acceptable. No evidence indicated incoming gasket material failure or deficient room sanitation.
Acceptable

Deficient

Acceptable

Shipment **SHIP-VC-1026-BOS-FRA** had a **high-temperature excursion** in the **Frankfurt airport controlled-transfer area** during transfer from the aircraft container to refrigerated road transport, when temperature rose above the validated **2.0–8.0 °C** range to a maximum of **10.7 °C** for **2 hr 30 min** from **15 Oct 2026 08:30 UTC to 11:00 UTC** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1; TL-VCL-1026.pdf, Page 1].

What happened:
- The investigation states the **probable cause** was that the **active air container remained at the controlled-transfer bay for 94 minutes beyond the validated handoff window after a ground-handler vehicle change** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- A **contributing factor** was that the **replacement refrigerated vehicle arrived after the scheduled connection window** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- The packaging was reported as **intact**, with **no opening or physical damage observed**, and proof of delivery recorded **no visible shipper damage** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2; EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].

Affected quantity:
- The affected inventory was **12 insulated cartons (4,800 units)** from **lot CLD-VCL-1026-A** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].

Can the 4,800 units be distributed?
- **Initially, no**: the units were placed in **physical quarantine** and labeled **“QUARANTINE – DO NOT DISTRIBUTE”** pending assessment [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].
- **Final disposition: yes**. The quality assessment concluded that the **recorded exposure remained within the approved stability allowance for lot CLD-VCL-1026-A** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- The final report explicitly states **“Released for distribution”**, quarantine was removed on **16 Oct 2026 18:10 UTC**, and the product **“may proceed through the authorized distribution channel”** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].

So, based on the retrieved evidence, the shipment experienced a transfer-delay-driven temperature excursion, but the specific affected lot **CLD-VCL-1026-A** was **formally released for distribution after quality review and customer disposition approval** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].

[{"annotations": [], "text": "Shipment **SHIP-VC-1026-BOS-FRA** had a **high-temperature excursion** in the **Frankfurt airport controlled-transfer area** during transfer from the aircraft container to refrigerated road transport, when temperature rose above the validated **2.0–8.0 °C** range to a maximum of **10.7 °C** for **2 hr 30 min** from **15 Oct 2026 08:30 UTC to 11:00 UTC** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1; TL-VCL-1026.pdf, Page 1].

What happened:
- The investigation states the **probable cause** was that the **active air container remained at the controlled-transfer bay for 94 minutes beyond the validated handoff window after a ground-handler vehicle change** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- A **contributing factor** was that the **replacement refrigerated vehicle arrived after the scheduled connection window** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- The packaging was reported as **intact**, with **no opening or physical damage observed**, and proof of delivery recorded **no visible shipper damage** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2; EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].

Affected quantity:
- The affected inventory was **12 insulated cartons (4,800 units)** from **lot CLD-VCL-1026-A** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].

Can the 4,800 units be distributed?
- **Initially, no**: the units were placed in **physical quarantine** and labeled **“QUARANTINE – DO NOT DISTRIBUTE”** pending assessment [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 1].
- **Final disposition: yes**. The quality assessment concluded that the **recorded exposure remained within the approved stability allowance for lot CLD-VCL-1026-A** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].
- The final report explicitly states **“Released for distribution”**, quarantine was removed on **16 Oct 2026 18:10 UTC**, and the product **“may proceed through the authorized distribution channel”** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].

So, based on the retrieved evidence, the shipment experienced a transfer-delay-driven temperature excursion, but the specific affected lot **CLD-VCL-1026-A** was **formally released for distribution after quality review and customer disposition approval** [EXC-VC-1026-04.pdf, Page 2].", "type": "output_text", "logprobs": []}]

datasource_item.query: Was lot LOT-MD-1026-A released, and should Caldova pay the $125,600 yield adjustment?
datasource_item.ground_truth: The Spanish certificate releases lot LOT-MD-1026-A. Actual released quantity was 7,200 kg and overall yield was 87.8%, within the approved 85-92% range. The $125,600 adjustment was calculated from an 8,000 kg forecast rather than actual released quantity, so Caldova should reject it.
datasource_item.sample.output_text:
Yes, lot **LOT-MD-1026-A was released**. The certificate of analysis states **“LIBERADO”** and says the lot **“queda aprobado para su suministro a Caldova Pharmaceuticals”** for lot **LOT-MD-1026-A** [COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 2]. The same COA identifies **LOT-MD-1026-A** with **released quantity 7,200 kg** [COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 1]. The yield worksheet also states the **released mass was 7,200 kg** and that the actual yield was **within the approved 85–92% range**, making it **the quantity eligible for lot billing** [YLD-MAW-1026.pdf, page 1].

Caldova **should not pay the $125,600 yield adjustment** based on the evidence retrieved. The invoice line itself says the charge was a **“Yield adjustment calculated from forecast API volume instead of actual lot yield”** and lists the amount as **$125,600.00** [INV-SUP-004-2026-10.pdf, page 1]. Caldova’s yield true-up assessment concludes **“Reject yield true-up”** and shows **“APPROVED INVOICE AMOUNT $0.00”** against the **claimed $125,600.00** [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 2]. The assessment explains that the forecast model used **8,000 kg** versus the actual released **7,200 kg**, calculating **800 kg × $157.00 = $125,600.00** [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 1]. It further states that the **released lot met its approved yield range** and that the **7,200 kg released quantity was already billed on invoice line L001** [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 1]. The yield worksheet separately confirms that the **released quantity is the quantity eligible for lot billing** [YLD-MAW-1026.pdf, page 1].

So, based on the records:
- **Released?** Yes — **LOT-MD-1026-A** was released for supply to Caldova [COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 2; COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 1].
- **Pay the $125,600 yield adjustment?** No — Caldova’s documented disposition is to **reject** that true-up and approve **$0.00** for that line [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 2].

Pharmaceutical quality system The site initiated deviation controls promptly and notified Caldova within the quality-agreement timeline. Premises and equipment BR-04 was orderly and appropriately segregated. TC-4 is positioned below an overhead return bend, limiting direct visual confirmation of gasket seating after assembly. No inspection mirror or borescope step was specified.
Deficient
Production and in-process controls Manufacturing records showed expected upstream controls and timely isolation. The closed transfer path was released to service without documented evidence that the required pressure-hold acceptance criterion had been met.
Deficient

Acceptable

Deficient
Materials, sanitation, and hygiene Gasket receipt, storage, status labeling, cleaning, and personnel gowning controls sampled were acceptable. No evidence indicated incoming gasket material failure or deficient room sanitation.

Yes, lot **LOT-MD-1026-A was released**. The certificate of analysis states **“LIBERADO”** and says the lot **“queda aprobado para su suministro a Caldova Pharmaceuticals”** for lot **LOT-MD-1026-A** [COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 2]. The same COA identifies **LOT-MD-1026-A** with **released quantity 7,200 kg** [COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 1]. The yield worksheet also states the **released mass was 7,200 kg** and that the actual yield was **within the approved 85–92% range**, making it **the quantity eligible for lot billing** [YLD-MAW-1026.pdf, page 1].

Caldova **should not pay the $125,600 yield adjustment** based on the evidence retrieved. The invoice line itself says the charge was a **“Yield adjustment calculated from forecast API volume instead of actual lot yield”** and lists the amount as **$125,600.00** [INV-SUP-004-2026-10.pdf, page 1]. Caldova’s yield true-up assessment concludes **“Reject yield true-up”** and shows **“APPROVED INVOICE AMOUNT $0.00”** against the **claimed $125,600.00** [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 2]. The assessment explains that the forecast model used **8,000 kg** versus the actual released **7,200 kg**, calculating **800 kg × $157.00 = $125,600.00** [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 1]. It further states that the **released lot met its approved yield range** and that the **7,200 kg released quantity was already billed on invoice line L001** [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 1]. The yield worksheet separately confirms that the **released quantity is the quantity eligible for lot billing** [YLD-MAW-1026.pdf, page 1].

So, based on the records:
- **Released?** Yes — **LOT-MD-1026-A** was released for supply to Caldova [COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 2; COA-MD-1026-A.pdf, page 1].
- **Pay the $125,600 yield adjustment?** No — Caldova’s documented disposition is to **reject** that true-up and approve **$0.00** for that line [YTA-MAW-1026-04.pdf, page 2].

datasource_item.query: Should Caldova approve BluePeak's $111,000 contamination-investigation charge? Cite the cause, inspection evidence, supply restriction, and corrective actions.
datasource_item.ground_truth: Caldova should reject BluePeak's $111,000 pass-through charge. The supplier-maintained TC-4 connection was reassembled with a pinched gasket and had no documented pressure-hold result. The scanned inspection report identifies two major deficiencies and conditionally blocks new BR-04 runs until required controls are in place and CAPA is verified.
datasource_item.sample.output_text:
No. Caldova should not approve BluePeak’s $111,000 contamination-investigation charge. The deviation review states the investigation was supplier-responsible, the pass-through fee should be rejected, and the approved invoice amount is $0.00 against the claimed $111,000.00 charge (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The invoice itself also labels this line as a contamination investigation billed where the deviation record indicates supplier-caused contamination (INV-SUP-009-2026-Q4.pdf, p. 1).

Cause: the root cause was that “a supplier-maintained transfer-hose connection was reassembled with a pinched gasket after preventive maintenance, compromising the closed path,” and the review found no sponsor material, instruction, or change contributed to the failure (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The inspection report independently confirmed the same root cause for the BP-1026-03 event at TC-4 (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3).

Inspection evidence: Caldova’s inspection confirmed four key facts: a positive sample was localized downstream of transfer connection TC-4, the retained upstream sample remained negative, gasket inspection found a visible compression fold, and the maintenance closeout omitted the required post-assembly pressure-hold result (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3). The inspection further documented that TC-4 was released for use even though the pressure-hold record had no result, reviewer confirmation, or objective evidence that acceptance criteria were met (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 4). It also found that maintenance qualification did not reliably prevent improper sanitary-gasket installation, including lack of a compensating visual-verification method for TC-4’s restricted orientation (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 5).

Supply restriction: this was not a general site shutdown. Caldova imposed conditional approval only: “no new Caldova BR-04 run may begin” until interim controls for gasket verification, witnessed pressure-hold testing, and Quality release are documented and accepted by Caldova (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 6). So the exact affected scope is new Caldova BR-04 runs, not all BluePeak supply.

Corrective actions: the deviation record lists these CAPAs—replace the TC-4 gasket and affected hose set; add witnessed pressure-hold verification after hose maintenance; and retrain maintenance technicians on gasket installation and closeout (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The inspection report adds committed systemic actions: revise the equipment-release workflow so pressure-hold results and Quality approval are hard-stop fields; execute a witnessed pressure-hold test before return to service; retrain and practically reassess all technicians assembling sanitary product-contact connections; add mirror or borescope confirmation plus second-person verification for restricted-orientation connections; and expand self-inspection sampling to linked evidence completeness and release-interlock effectiveness (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 6).

So based on the retrieved evidence, Caldova should reject BluePeak’s $111,000 charge because the contamination cause and investigation responsibility were assigned to BluePeak, not Caldova (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available; GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3).

queries: Should Caldova approve BluePeak's $111,000 contamination-investigation charge? Cite the cause, inspection evidence, supply restriction, and corrective actions.

The deviation review states the investigation was supplier-responsible, the pass-through fee should be rejected, and the approved invoice amount is $0.00 against the claimed $111,000.00 charge (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The invoice itself also labels this line as a contamination investigation billed where the deviation record indicates supplier-caused contamination (INV-SUP-009-2026-Q4.pdf, p. 1).

Cause: the root cause was that “a supplier-maintained transfer-hose connection was reassembled with a pinched gasket after preventive maintenance, compromising the closed path,” and the review found no sponsor material, instruction, or change contributed to the failure (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The inspection report independently confirmed the same root cause for the BP-1026-03 event at TC-4 (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3).

Inspection evidence: Caldova’s inspection confirmed four key facts: a positive sample was localized downstream of transfer connection TC-4, the retained upstream sample remained negative, gasket inspection found a visible compression fold, and the maintenance closeout omitted the required post-assembly pressure-hold result (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3). The inspection further documented that TC-4 was released for use even though the pressure-hold record had no result, reviewer confirmation, or objective evidence that acceptance criteria were met (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 4). It also found that maintenance qualification did not reliably prevent improper sanitary-gasket installation, including lack of a compensating visual-verification method for TC-4’s restricted orientation (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 5).

Supply restriction: this was not a general site shutdown. Caldova imposed conditional approval only: “no new Caldova BR-04 run may begin” until interim controls for gasket verification, witnessed pressure-hold testing, and Quality release are documented and accepted by Caldova (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 6). So the exact affected scope is new Caldova BR-04 runs, not all BluePeak supply.

Corrective actions: the deviation record lists these CAPAs—replace the TC-4 gasket and affected hose set; add witnessed pressure-hold verification after hose maintenance; and retrain maintenance technicians on gasket installation and closeout (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The inspection report adds committed systemic actions: revise the equipment-release workflow so pressure-hold results and Quality approval are hard-stop fields; execute a witnessed pressure-hold test before return to service; retrain and practically reassess all technicians assembling sanitary product-contact connections; add mirror or borescope confirmation plus second-person verification for restricted-orientation connections; and expand self-inspection sampling to linked evidence completeness and release-interlock effectiveness (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 6).

So based on the retrieved evidence, Caldova should reject BluePeak’s $111,000 charge because the contamination cause and investigation responsibility were assigned to BluePeak, not Caldova (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available; GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3).

[{"annotations": [], "text": "No. Caldova should not approve BluePeak’s $111,000 contamination-investigation charge. The deviation review states the investigation was supplier-responsible, the pass-through fee should be rejected, and the approved invoice amount is $0.00 against the claimed $111,000.00 charge (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The invoice itself also labels this line as a contamination investigation billed where the deviation record indicates supplier-caused contamination (INV-SUP-009-2026-Q4.pdf, p. 1).

Cause: the root cause was that “a supplier-maintained transfer-hose connection was reassembled with a pinched gasket after preventive maintenance, compromising the closed path,” and the review found no sponsor material, instruction, or change contributed to the failure (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The inspection report independently confirmed the same root cause for the BP-1026-03 event at TC-4 (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3).

Inspection evidence: Caldova’s inspection confirmed four key facts: a positive sample was localized downstream of transfer connection TC-4, the retained upstream sample remained negative, gasket inspection found a visible compression fold, and the maintenance closeout omitted the required post-assembly pressure-hold result (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3). The inspection further documented that TC-4 was released for use even though the pressure-hold record had no result, reviewer confirmation, or objective evidence that acceptance criteria were met (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 4). It also found that maintenance qualification did not reliably prevent improper sanitary-gasket installation, including lack of a compensating visual-verification method for TC-4’s restricted orientation (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 5).

Supply restriction: this was not a general site shutdown. Caldova imposed conditional approval only: “no new Caldova BR-04 run may begin” until interim controls for gasket verification, witnessed pressure-hold testing, and Quality release are documented and accepted by Caldova (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 6). So the exact affected scope is new Caldova BR-04 runs, not all BluePeak supply.

Corrective actions: the deviation record lists these CAPAs—replace the TC-4 gasket and affected hose set; add witnessed pressure-hold verification after hose maintenance; and retrain maintenance technicians on gasket installation and closeout (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available). The inspection report adds committed systemic actions: revise the equipment-release workflow so pressure-hold results and Quality approval are hard-stop fields; execute a witnessed pressure-hold test before return to service; retrain and practically reassess all technicians assembling sanitary product-contact connections; add mirror or borescope confirmation plus second-person verification for restricted-orientation connections; and expand self-inspection sampling to linked evidence completeness and release-interlock effectiveness (GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 6).

So based on the retrieved evidence, Caldova should reject BluePeak’s $111,000 charge because the contamination cause and investigation responsibility were assigned to BluePeak, not Caldova (DEV-BPB-1026.pdf, page not available; GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01.pdf, p. 3).", "type": "output_text", "logprobs": []}]

datasource_item.ground_truth: Caldova should reject Meridian API Works' $125,600 forecast-based yield adjustment, BluePeak Biologics' $111,000 supplier-caused contamination-investigation charge, and Keystone Device Assembly's $86,450 unsupported excess-scrap charge. datasource_item.sample.output_text:
Based on the retrieved invoice-assessment records, Caldova should reject these disputed charges:

- **BluePeak Biologics invoice line INV-SUP-009-2026-Q4-L004** for the **contamination investigation fee** of **$111,000.00**. The invoice line bills a contamination investigation where the deviation indicates supplier-caused contamination, and the linked disposition states: **“Supplier responsible; reject pass-through investigation fee”** with **approved invoice amount $0.00** and **claimed $111,000.00**. The affected run was **BP-1026-03**, and the issue was tied to **transfer connection TC-4**. (INV-SUP-009-2026-Q4, p.1; DEV-BPB-1026, page not available; GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01, p.3)

- **Keystone Device Assembly invoice line INV-SUP-010-2026-10-L004** for the **excess scrap charge** of **$86,450.00**. The invoice line bills **component scrap above 1.5%**, and the disposition states: **“Disallow excess scrap charge”** with **approved invoice amount $0.00** and **claimed $86,450.00**. The nonconformance record says the excess scrap was attributable to supplier process controls, not sponsor cause. (INV-SUP-010-2026-10, p.1; NCR-KDA-1026-07, page not available)

- **Meridian API Works invoice line INV-SUP-004-2026-10-L004** for the **yield adjustment / yield true-up** of **$125,600.00**. The invoice bills a **yield adjustment calculated from forecast API volume instead of actual lot yield**, and the assessment states: **“Reject yield true-up”** with **approved invoice amount $0.00** and **claimed $125,600.00**. The supporting reconciliation says the **7,200 kg released quantity was already billed on invoice line L001**. (INV-SUP-004-2026-10, p.1; YTA-MAW-1026-04, page not available)

**Total avoided cost:**  
$111,000.00 + $86,450.00 + $125,600.00 = **$323,050.00** (DEV-BPB-1026, page not available; NCR-KDA-1026-07, page not available; YTA-MAW-1026-04, page not available)

I do **not** have enough retrieved evidence to say any other invoice charges should be rejected. Some invoices contain potentially questionable line descriptions, but without a linked disposition or assessment record in the retrieved evidence, I cannot conclude they should be rejected.

Objective evidence: Blank pressure-hold result; work-order closure audit trail; run BP-1026-03 equipment-release entry. The invoice line bills a contamination investigation where the deviation indicates supplier-caused contamination, and the linked disposition states: **“Supplier responsible; reject pass-through investigation fee”** with **approved invoice amount $0.00** and **claimed $111,000.00**. The affected run was **BP-1026-03**, and the issue was tied to **transfer connection TC-4**. (INV-SUP-009-2026-Q4, p.1; DEV-BPB-1026, page not available; GMP-INS-BPB-2027-01, p.3)

- **Keystone Device Assembly invoice line INV-SUP-010-2026-10-L004** for the **excess scrap charge** of **$86,450.00**. The invoice line bills **component scrap above 1.5%**, and the disposition states: **“Disallow excess scrap charge”** with **approved invoice amount $0.00** and **claimed $86,450.00**. The nonconformance record says the excess scrap was attributable to supplier process controls, not sponsor cause. (INV-SUP-010-2026-10, p.1; NCR-KDA-1026-07, page not available)

- **Meridian API Works invoice line INV-SUP-004-2026-10-L004** for the **yield adjustment / yield true-up** of **$125,600.00**. **Total avoided cost:**  
$111,000.00 + $86,450.00 + $125,600.00 = **$323,050.00** (DEV-BPB-1026, page not available; NCR-KDA-1026-07, page not available; YTA-MAW-1026-04, page not available)
